claims.claim: AEP controls a scarce grid bottleneck between accelerating data-center/industrial electricity demand and delivered power: its large transmission footprint plus regulated generation/distribution investment convert signed large-load demand into rate-base opportunity subject to regulatory and buildout execution.

causalEdges.mechanism: signed large-load commitments require grid interconnection and capacity additions
causalEdges.falsifier: contracted load cancellations or interconnection delays materially reduce realized load

causalEdges.mechanism: approved capital enters rate base and earns regulated returns
causalEdges.falsifier: regulators disallow material costs or affordability constraints prevent timely recovery

risks.risk: Generation availability, turbine supply, permitting and regulatory approvals can become successor bottlenecks after transmission demand is identified.

unknowns.unknown: Timing and utilization profile of the full 69 GW contracted load portfolio remains uncertain.

claims.claim: The load-growth thesis remains defensible but financing and recovery risk are material: AEP's Q2 filing shows increased long-term and short-term debt issuance and common-stock issuance under its ATM program while it pursues a $78B five-year capital plan.

risks.risk: Capital intensity requires substantial debt/equity financing; higher funding costs or weaker credit metrics can erode shareholder economics.
Large-load contracts still require generation, transmission, permits and regulatory cost recovery; signed demand is not equivalent to realized energized load.
Affordability pressure can constrain rate recovery even when infrastructure need is genuine.

contradictions.contradiction: AEP raised full-year guidance despite Q2 operating EPS declining YoY, so growth expectations depend materially on future capital deployment and load conversion rather than current-quarter momentum alone.

unknowns.unknown: Customer-by-customer concentration and cancellation protections across the 69 GW portfolio are not fully disclosed in current evidence.
